Fit the Poisson-multinomial model

Source: R/pre_proc.R
fit_model.Rd

Builds the model formula with parse_form() and fits it with either brms (Bayesian, backend = "brms") or sdmTMB (maximum likelihood, backend = "TMB"). Counts per stratum and bin are modelled as Poisson with log(n) as offset, so that the implied within-stratum proportions follow a multinomial-logit model (see vignette("ComPoM") for the model equations).

Usage

fit_model(
  ffx_form,
  re_form = NULL,
  cvars = NULL,
  spl = "2D",
  knots = "c(5,10)",
  data = NULL,
  dist = "poisson",
  chains = 4,
  threads = NULL,
  cores = min(chains, parallel::detectCores()),
  backend = "brms",
  brms_backend = "rstan",
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  mtd = 10,
  ad = 0.8,
  thin = 2,
  refresh = 10,
  add_preds = FALSE,
  mesh = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  share_spatial_sd = TRUE,
  share_spatiotemporal_sd = TRUE,
  spatiotemporal = TRUE,
  coords = c("x", "y"),
  priors = NULL,
  newton_loops = 1
)

Arguments

ffx_form

A character string of primary fixed-effect variables (RHS), e.g. "Year". Passed to parse_form().

re_form

A character string of nuisance random-effect variables, e.g. "Season + Gear". These become (1|bin:var) IID intercepts. NULL = none.

cvars

Continuous covariate(s) to be fitted as smooths with bin; see spl.

spl

Smooth type for cvars: "2D", "by_factor" or "by"; see parse_form(). "2D" is unreliable with backend = "TMB" (non-positive-definite Hessian); use "by_factor" there.

knots

Basis dimension(s) for the cvars smooth, as a character string (e.g. "4" or "c(5,10)" for spl = "2D").

data

Prepared data frame from data_prep().

dist

Response family passed to brms::brm() as family: a family name (default "poisson") or family object such as poisson() (brms backend only; the TMB backend always uses poisson()).

chains, cores, threads

Number of MCMC chains, cores and within-chain threads (brms backend only). By default, one core is used per chain (up to the number of available cores) and no within-chain threading.

backend

the backend used for model fitting: "brms" or "TMB".

brms_backend

Stan interface used by brms ("rstan" or "cmdstanr").

iter, warmup, thin

MCMC iterations, warm-up iterations and thinning (brms). For the TMB backend these only set the number of simulation draws used downstream, nsim = (iter - warmup) / thin.

mtd, ad

Stan max_treedepth and adapt_delta (brms only).

refresh

Stan progress refresh interval (brms only).

add_preds

Add posterior predictive draws for the fitted data, required by post_pred_group(). Can be slow.

mesh

An sdmTMB mesh object created with make_mesh() (TMB backend only)

time

Column name for time (year) variable (TMB backend only)

share_spatial_sd

Share spatial SD across bins (TMB backend only)

share_spatiotemporal_sd

Share spatiotemporal SD across bins (TMB backend only)

spatiotemporal

Include spatio-temporal fields (one per bin and time step) in addition to the spatial fields (TMB backend with a mesh only). FALSE fits spatial fields only; time is still required, as it is used for prediction.

coords

Character vector of coordinate column names (TMB backend only)

priors

An sdmTMBpriors() object for regularisation (TMB non-spatial backend only; currently not passed to the spatial fit). Useful when the design matrix is sparse (e.g. normal(0, 2) on fixed effects).

newton_loops

Number of extra Newton optimisation steps after initial fit (TMB non-spatial only). Default 1. Increase to 2-3 for difficult convergence. For spatial fits use sdmTMB::run_extra_optimization() on $model.

Value

An object of class ComPoM: a list with the fitted model (model, a brmsfit or sdmTMB object), the model data (data), the number of draws used downstream (nsim), posterior predictive draws (preds, or NULL), and the settings needed by the post-processing functions (mesh, spatial_varying, time, coords, re_vars, cvars).

Details

With backend = "TMB" and a mesh, the model adds one spatial Gaussian random field per bin and one spatio-temporal field per bin and time step (set up with sdmTMB::make_category_svc()). Set spatiotemporal = FALSE to fit the spatial fields only.

With backend = "brms", fixed effects receive a student_t(10, 0, 1) prior. With backend = "TMB", uncertainty in downstream functions is obtained from nsim draws from the approximate joint sampling distribution of the parameters.

See also

data_prep(), scale_comps(), Fx_plot(), vignette("ComPoM")

Examples

dat <- data_prep(ex_comp, c("Year", "Season", "Vessel", "trip"), "length", "count")

# maximum likelihood fit: Year as effect of interest, Season and Vessel as
# nuisance random effects
fit <- fit_model(
  ffx_form = "Year", re_form = "Season + Vessel",
  data = dat, backend = "TMB", iter = 300, warmup = 100, thin = 2
)
#> Model formula: tot_by_bin ~ 0 + bin + factor(Year):bin + (1 | bin:Season) + (1 | bin:Vessel)
class(fit)
#> [1] "ComPoM"

# \donttest{
# Bayesian fit with brms (compiles a Stan model; slow)
fit_b <- fit_model(
  ffx_form = "Year", re_form = "Season + Vessel", data = dat,
  backend = "brms", chains = 2, iter = 400, warmup = 200, thin = 1
)
#> Model formula: tot_by_bin ~ offset(log(n)) + 0 + bin + factor(Year):bin + (1 | bin:Season) + (1 | bin:Vessel)
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Start sampling
#> Warning: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess
#> Warning: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess
#> Converged (all Rhat < 1.05): TRUE
# }
